test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 12 Dec 2022 Shift 4)
subject: general
question: A conical vessel, whose internal radius is 20 cm and height is 27 cm, is full of water. If this water is poured into a cylindrical vessel with internal radius 15 cm, what will be the height to which the water rises in it?
solution:
**Given:**

Internal radius of vessel = 20 cm

Height of vessel = 27 cm

**Formula used: **

Radius = r and h = height and l = slant = height

Volume of cone = 1/3 × πr²h

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

**Calculation: **

Volume of conical vessel = (1/3 × π × 20² × 27) cm³

Volume of cylindrical vessel = (π × 15² × height) cm³

Then, (1/3 × π × 202 × 27) = (π × 152 × height)

Height of cylindrical vessel = 16 cm

**∴ water rises by 16 cm.**
